general-excavation|mechanical-open-cut-e.descripcion: Mechanical open-cut excavation for general bulk excavation, reducing levels or forming a platform, with an excavator or skid steer loader, in ground of medium consistency. Includes setting out and marking the final level, excavating in layers, stockpiling the material on site or loading it directly onto a lorry, hand trimming of the edges and slopes, and survey control of the level achieved. It does not include cartage of the surplus material to a spoil site, which is priced in the earthworks haulage subsection. Measured by the theoretical volume of excavation to the design levels.

general-excavation|excavation-in-hard-ma.titulo: Excavation in hard material or rock
general-excavation|excavation-in-hard-ma.descripcion: Excavation in ground of high compaction, cemented material or rock, with a hydraulic breaker mounted on an excavator, with a hand-held pneumatic breaker for the corners. It applies where the output of conventional excavation falls below what is acceptable, a circumstance that must be recorded on site to justify the change of item. Includes breaking up the material, extracting and stockpiling it, trimming the sides and bottom, and controlling vibration where there are adjoining buildings. It does not include cartage of the surplus material to a spoil site, which is priced in the earthworks haulage subsection. Measured by the theoretical volume of excavation to the design dimensions.

general-excavation|excavation-for-a-sept.titulo: Excavation for a septic tank, gully or buried tank
general-excavation|excavation-for-a-sept.descripcion: Excavation to receive a septic tank, gully, buried water tank or similar, to the design dimensions plus the working space needed for installation and subsequent backfilling around it. Includes setting out, excavation by mechanical means with hand trimming, trimming the bottom to the exact bearing level, checking the stability of the sides and sheeting them where the depth requires it, and signing and covering the void while it remains open. It does not include cartage of the surplus material to a spoil site, which is priced in the earthworks haulage subsection. Measured by the theoretical volume of excavation to the design dimensions.

general-excavation|trimming-and-compacti.titulo: Trimming and compaction of the bottom of an excavation
general-excavation|trimming-and-compacti.descripcion: Trimming, fine trimming and compaction of the bottom of the excavation, leaving it at the exact level, flat and with the density required to receive the foundation or the base of the paving. Includes removal of loose and disturbed material from the bottom, hand trimming to the design level, moisture conditioning of the ground to optimum moisture content and compaction with a vibrating plate or rammer depending on the width available. Measured by the area of the bottom actually trimmed.

general-excavation|hand-excavation-indoo.descripcion: Hand excavation inside an existing building, for reducing levels, constructing strengthening foundations or running buried services. Output is far lower than for open-cut excavation because of the lack of room to manoeuvre, the impossibility of using plant and the need to carry the material out by hand through the building. Includes setting out, protecting the circulation areas, excavating in layers with pick and shovel, bagging the material and carrying it to the external stockpile. Disposal is not included.

general-excavation|excavation-for-a-base.descripcion: Excavation for a basement, including removal of the spoil. Includes excavation and stockpiling. Measured per cubic metre excavated.

general-excavation|excavation-to-formati.descripcion: Excavation to formation level for levelling the site. Includes excavation and stockpiling. Measured per cubic metre excavated.

lineas.nombre: Demolition consumables: hammer bits and chisels, cutting discs and scraper blades.

general-excavation|open-cut-excavation-w.descripcion: Mechanical open-cut excavation with the material cast to one side. Includes excavation and stockpiling of the material removed. Measured per cubic metre excavated.

lineas.nombre: Demolition consumables: hammer bits and chisels, cutting discs and scraper blades.

6 m3 tipper lorry with driver, for hauling debris to the landfill.

trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.titulo: Hand excavation of a foundation trench
trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.descripcion: Hand excavation of a trench or pit for foundations, in ground of medium consistency, to the level and to the design dimensions. It is the usual solution on refurbishment work and extensions where plant cannot get in or the volume does not justify it. Includes setting out of the trench, excavating in layers with pick and shovel, stockpiling the material far enough back from the edge not to overload it, trimming the sides and bottom, and getting the material out to the loading point. It does not include cartage of the surplus material to a spoil site, which is priced in the earthworks haulage subsection. Measured by the theoretical volume of excavation to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Demolition consumables: hammer bits and chisels, cutting discs and scraper blades.
Skilled labourer.
Labourer.

trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.titulo: Mechanical excavation of a foundation trench
trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.descripcion: Mechanical excavation of a trench or pit for foundations with an excavator, in ground of medium consistency, to the level and to the design dimensions. Includes setting out, excavation by machine, stockpiling the material far enough back from the edge, hand trimming of the sides and bottom that the machine cannot achieve, and watching during excavation so that work stops if unforeseen buried services are found. It does not include cartage of the surplus material to a spoil site, which is priced in the earthworks haulage subsection. Measured by the theoretical volume of excavation to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Demolition consumables: hammer bits and chisels, cutting discs and scraper blades.
Excavator or skid steer loader with hydraulic breaker and operator.
Skilled labourer.
Labourer.

trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.titulo: Hand excavation of a trench for buried services
trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.descripcion: Hand excavation of a narrow trench for laying water pipes, drains or buried electrical conduits, to the fall required by the service. It is done by hand precisely because in built-up areas the risk of striking an existing service makes the machine inadvisable. Includes setting out of the line, excavating in layers under continuous watch, stockpiling the material alongside the trench, trimming the bottom to the required fall and keeping the trench signed while it remains open. It does not include cartage of the surplus material to a spoil site, which is priced in the earthworks haulage subsection. Measured by the theoretical volume of excavation to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Demolition consumables: hammer bits and chisels, cutting discs and scraper blades.

trenches-shafts-and-localised-excavation.descripcion: Trench sheeting to the sides of the excavation with timber planks and struts, to support the ground and allow safe work inside. It is mandatory from the depth at which the ground stops being self-supporting, and its absence is the main cause of serious accidents in trenches. Includes installing the sheeting as the excavation advances and never afterwards, placing the planks and struts with the wedging required, daily inspection of the assembly and after every rainfall, and staged removal as the backfill proceeds. Measured by the area of trench face actually sheeted.

lineas.nombre: Timber plank and strut, for trench propping, depreciated over the number of uses.
Nails, screws and general-purpose site fixings.

Skilled labourer.

fills-and-compaction|backfill-and-compac.titulo: Backfill and compaction with material from the site
fills-and-compaction|backfill-and-compac.descripcion: Backfill to trenches, behind walls or to reduced levels with the material arising from the excavation itself, provided it is suitable through containing no organic matter or compressible elements, spread and compacted in layers not exceeding 20 cm. Includes selecting and rough screening the stockpiled material, spreading it in layers, moisture conditioning to optimum moisture content, compacting each layer with a rammer or vibrating plate depending on the space, and checking the final level. Measured by the volume of compacted fill to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Water, for mixing, wetting fill and compaction.

fills-and-compaction|backfill-and-compac.titulo: Backfill and compaction with imported granular fill
fills-and-compaction|backfill-and-compac.descripcion: Backfill with selected imported granular fill, such as natural run of crusher, spread and compacted in layers not exceeding 20 cm, used where the material on site does not meet the requirements. Includes supply and placing of the material, spreading it in layers, moisture conditioning to optimum moisture content, compacting each layer to the specified density and checking the final level. Measured by the volume of compacted fill to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Selected imported granular fill, natural gravel type, placed for compacted backfill.

fills-and-compaction|backfill-of-a-servi.titulo: Backfill of a services trench with sand
fills-and-compaction|backfill-of-a-servi.descripcion: Backfill of a services trench with washed sand, forming the bedding beneath the pipe and the surround up to 20 cm above its crown, to protect it from point loads and from contact with coarse material. Includes supply and placing of the sand, forming the bed to the fall of the service, filling the sides and over the top in layers with careful hand compaction so as not to displace or damage the pipe, and laying warning tape over the surround. Measured by the volume of sand actually placed.

lineas.nombre: Washed river sand, placed, for bedding and trench backfill.
Warning signs, hazard tape and cones, for demarcating the works.
Water, for mixing, wetting fill and compaction.

fills-and-compaction|compacted-crushed-s.descripcion: Crushed stone base spread and compacted beneath floors, pavements or external paving, acting as a drainage and load spreading layer and breaking the capillary rise of moisture into the floor. Includes supply and placing of the stone, spreading it in 15 cm layers, choking with fine material where the surface has to be closed, compaction with a vibrating plate and checking the final level and regularity. Measured by the volume of compacted base to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Crushed stone, standard grading, placed, for bases and drainage.
Water, for mixing, wetting fill and compaction.
Vibratory vibrating plate, for compacting surfaces and bases.

Labourer.

fills-and-compaction|levelling-and-compa.titulo: Levelling and compaction of the ground
fills-and-compaction|levelling-and-compa.descripcion: Levelling and compaction of the surface of the ground after clearing or filling, leaving it at the level and fall of the design and with the density needed to receive the next layer. Includes going over the surface, cutting off the high spots and making up the low ones, moisture conditioning to optimum moisture content, compaction with a vibrating plate in crossed passes and checking levels and falls with a laser level. Measured by the area actually levelled and compacted.

lineas.nombre: Water, for mixing, wetting fill and compaction.
Vibratory vibrating plate, for compacting surfaces and bases.
Self-levelling laser level and measuring equipment for setting out.

fills-and-compaction|backfill-with-reuse.descripcion: Backfill with reused excavated material, after screening. Includes spreading and compaction. Measured per cubic metre filled.

loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|hand-loadin.titulo: Hand loading and cartage of surplus spoil to a spoil site
loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|hand-loadin.descripcion: Hand loading of surplus excavated material onto a tipper lorry and cartage to a licensed spoil site, including the tipping fee, based on an average distance of 25 km. It is used where the stockpile cannot be reached by loading plant. Includes loading onto the vehicle by shovel, sheeting and securing the load to prevent spillage in transit, cartage, tipping and cleaning of the loading area. Measured by the volume of bulked material actually removed.

lineas.nombre: Tipping charge for disposal of spoil and excavated material at a licensed site.
6 m3 tipper lorry with driver, for hauling debris to the landfill.

loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|mechanical-.titulo: Mechanical loading and cartage of surplus spoil to a spoil site
loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|mechanical-.descripcion: Mechanical loading of surplus excavated material with an excavator onto a tipper lorry and cartage to a licensed spoil site, including the tipping fee, based on an average distance of 25 km. Includes loading with the machine, sheeting and securing the load, cartage, tipping, hand trimming of the residual stockpile and cleaning of the loading area. Measured by the volume of bulked material actually removed.

lineas.nombre: Tipping charge for disposal of spoil and excavated material at a licensed site.
Excavator or skid steer loader with hydraulic breaker and operator.
6 m3 tipper lorry with driver, for hauling debris to the landfill.

loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|temporary-s.titulo: Temporary stockpiling of soil on site for reuse
loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|temporary-s.descripcion: Internal movement and temporary stockpiling on site of excavated material suitable for reuse in the later backfill, avoiding the double cost of tipping it and then buying imported fill. Includes moving the material to the stockpile, heaping it with a stable batter and clear of the edges of the excavation, covering it with plastic sheeting to prevent washing out by rain and a rise in moisture content, and recovering it later for the backfill. Measured by the volume of material actually stockpiled.

lineas.nombre: Polyethylene sheet, for protecting furniture, screening off areas and dust barriers.
Excavator or skid steer loader with hydraulic breaker and operator.
Labourer.

loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|supply-and-.titulo: Supply and cartage of imported fill to the site
loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|supply-and-.descripcion: Supply of imported granular fill from a quarry or approved supplier and its cartage and tipping on site at the stockpile indicated. Includes checking the grading and cleanliness of the material on arrival, rejecting the load if it does not comply, tipping at the agreed point and recording the volumes received against the delivery tickets. Measured by the volume of material actually received on site.

lineas.nombre: Selected imported granular fill, natural gravel type, placed for compacted backfill.
6 m3 tipper lorry with driver, for hauling debris to the landfill.
Labourer.

loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|internal-mo.titulo: Internal movement of material by wheelbarrow
loading-and-haulage-of-spoil|internal-mo.descripcion: Internal movement of spoil, debris or bulk material by wheelbarrow, from the work face to the stockpile or loading point, on work where plant cannot get in. Includes preparing and protecting the route, loading by shovel, carting over the average distance on site, tipping it neatly at the stockpile and continuous cleaning of the route, which in an occupied building is mandatory and takes real time. Measured by the volume of material actually moved.

lineas.nombre: Site protection with plastic sheet, corrugated board and masking tape.
Heavy-duty woven polypropylene sack, for removing debris by hand.

compaction-and-levelling-of-foundation-b.descripcion: Levelling and compaction of the bottom of the footing excavation. Includes levelling and compaction. Measured per square metre constructed.

spread-footings|5-cm-blinding-beneath-fo.descripcion: Blinding of 5 cm average thickness, poured over the bottom of the excavation before the footing is reinforced. It serves a purpose of execution rather than a structural one: it separates the steel from the ground, stops soil contaminating the structural concrete and gives a clean level surface on which to set out and stand the spacers. Includes going over and compacting the bottom, pouring and spreading the concrete, screeding it level and marking the centre lines of the footing on the hardened slab. Measured by the area actually constructed.

spread-footings|reinforcement-in-footing.descripcion: Supply, cutting, bending, assembly and placing of deformed bar reinforcement of 4,200 kg/cm² yield strength to footings and foundation bases, to the bending schedules. Includes cutting and bending on site or taking delivery of the steel pre-bent, assembling the mats tied with wire at every intersection around the perimeter and at alternate intersections within, placing spacers to give the specified cover on every face, bracing the cage so that it cannot move during the pour and checking the schedule before the concrete is authorized. Measured by the weight of steel actually placed, excluding offcuts and laps not allowed for in the schedule.

spread-footings|formwork-and-stripping-t.descripcion: Formwork to the sides of a footing using wood panels with props and bracing, and its subsequent stripping. Includes setting out and erecting the panels, checking the squareness, plumb and dimensions before the pour, the propping and bracing that stops the formwork opening under the thrust of the wet concrete, applying release agent, careful stripping once the necessary strength has been reached, and cleaning and stacking the panels for reuse. Measured by the area of formwork in contact with the concrete.

lineas.nombre: Timber formwork with its props and bracing, depreciated over the number of uses.
Nails, screws and general-purpose site fixings.
Formwork release agent, to ease striking and protect the timber.
Tradesperson formwork carpenter.
Labourer.

spread-footings|concrete-for-a-pad-found.descripcion: Ready-mixed concrete of 210 kg/cm² strength poured into a pad foundation, including compaction by vibration and curing. Includes the prior check of the cage, of the formwork and of the cover, taking delivery of and checking the concrete on arrival and rejecting the load if the slump is not right, pouring in layers avoiding segregation, compacting with an internal vibrator without touching the cage or the formwork, screeding the top face, curing over the first few days and taking test cubes where quality control requires it. Measured by the theoretical volume to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Ready-mixed concrete, 210 kg/cm2 (approx. 21 MPa), placed.
Membrane-forming curing compound for concrete, retaining the mixing water.
Internal concrete vibrator with motor, for compacting concrete.

spread-footings|concrete-for-a-strip-fou.descripcion: Ready-mixed concrete of 210 kg/cm² strength poured into a strip foundation under a wall or a line of columns, including compaction by vibration and curing. Pouring into a continuous trench gives a slightly better output than pad foundations because of the continuity of the working face. Includes the prior check of the cage and of the cover, taking delivery of and checking the concrete, pouring in layers, compacting with an internal vibrator, screeding the top face to the level specified and curing over the first few days. Measured by the theoretical volume to the design dimensions.

lineas.nombre: Ready-mixed concrete, 210 kg/cm2 (approx. 21 MPa), placed.
Membrane-forming curing compound for concrete, retaining the mixing water.
Internal concrete vibrator with motor, for compacting concrete.

spread-footings|reinforced-concrete-pede.titulo: Reinforced concrete pedestal on a foundation
spread-footings|reinforced-concrete-pede.descripcion: Reinforced concrete pedestal of 210 kg/cm² strength rising from the footing and taking the bearing of the column up to the commencing level, including its formwork, pouring and curing. Includes setting out on the footing, erecting and plumbing the formwork with bracing on all four faces, checking that the starter bars are in position and have the lap length specified, pouring and vibrating in layers, stripping and curing. It does not include the reinforcement, which is priced by weight. Measured by the theoretical volume to the design dimensions.

spread-footings|concrete-base-or-plinth-.titulo: Concrete base or plinth for equipment or machinery
spread-footings|concrete-base-or-plinth-.descripcion: Construction of a reinforced concrete plinth or base to carry equipment, machinery, tanks or minor structures, with its formwork, reinforcement, pour and provision for anchor bolts. Includes excavation and compaction of the bottom, the formwork, the reinforcement, placing the anchor bolt template before the pour, which is what guarantees that the equipment beds down without forced adjustment, pouring and vibrating, curing and striking. Measured per unit constructed.

spread-footings|underpinning-of-an-exist.descripcion: Underpinning of an existing footing in bays, to widen its bearing area or to lower its level where settlement has appeared or where the load on the structure is being increased. It is carried out in alternate bays and never continuously: excavating under the whole footing at once leaves it without support and causes the collapse it is meant to prevent. Includes the study and the fixing of the order of the bays, excavation in alternate bays, the formwork, the reinforcement tied into the existing footing with chemical anchors, pouring with shrinkage-compensating mortar, wedging against the existing footing and waiting before the next bay is opened. Measured by the length actually underpinned.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|su.titulo: Surface repair of concrete with structural mortar
reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|su.descripcion: Repair of concrete damaged by honeycombing, spalling or carbonation, by cutting out the area and reinstating with a thixotropic structural repair mortar, 3 cm average thickness. Includes defining the area with a square perimeter cut to avoid feather edges that come away, hacking out the loose concrete back to sound concrete, cleaning and saturating the substrate, applying the bonding coat, reinstating the mortar in layers respecting the maximum thickness per layer and curing the material applied. Measured by the area actually repaired.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|pa.descripcion: Cleaning and treatment of corroded reinforcement exposed after the concrete has been cut out, by brushing to a suitable standard of cleanliness and applying a passivating coating with inhibitor. It is the step that decides whether the repair lasts: if the mortar is reinstated over rusted steel, corrosion continues underneath and blows the cover again within a few years. Includes exposing the steel around its whole perimeter leaving a gap behind the bar, removing the rust with a wire brush and by grinding, assessing the loss of section and notifying the designer if it exceeds what is permissible, and applying two coats of passivator. Measured by the area of element actually treated.

lineas.nombre: Cement-based passivating coating with inhibitor, to protect corroded reinforcement.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|in.titulo: Injection of cracks in concrete with epoxy resin
reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|in.descripcion: Sealing and restoring the monolithic action of cracks in concrete elements by injecting low viscosity epoxy resin through injection ports. Includes mapping beforehand and recording the width and the run of the cracks, determining whether the crack is live or dormant, since injecting a moving crack with a rigid resin makes it reappear alongside the seal, cleaning the run, fitting the ports and sealing the surface of the crack, injecting progressively from port to port until it appears at the next, setting, and removing the ports and the seal and making good the surface. Measured by the length of crack actually injected.

lineas.nombre: Two-component epoxy resin, for chemical anchoring of bars and for crack injection.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|st.titulo: Structural strengthening with carbon fibre fabric
reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|st.descripcion: Strengthening of a structural concrete element by bonding carbon fibre fabric with a saturating epoxy resin. It adds flexural or shear capacity with almost no added weight and no change to the geometry, which makes it ideal in refurbishment where the section cannot be increased. Includes preparing and rubbing down the substrate to a flat surface free of laitance, rounding the arrises over which the fabric has to bend, priming, applying the saturating resin, laying the fabric in the direction of the tension and rolling out the air bubbles, the second coat of resin and curing. Measured by the area of fabric actually applied.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|ja.titulo: Jacketing of a reinforced concrete column
reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|ja.descripcion: Strengthening of an existing column by reinforced concrete jacketing, increasing its section with a perimeter layer of concrete with its own reinforcement, tied to the original core. Includes propping the structure beforehand to take the load off the column, hacking the existing surface to provide a bond, drilling and chemically anchoring the dowels that stitch the jacket to the core, the longitudinal reinforcement and the confinement links, the formwork, pouring with shrinkage-compensating concrete or a fluid mortar given the small thickness, curing and the staged removal of the propping. Measured by the length of column actually jacketed.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|ch.titulo: Chemical anchoring of a steel bar in concrete
reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|ch.descripcion: Anchoring of a steel bar into an existing concrete element with two-component epoxy resin injected into the hole, to connect new elements to the existing structure. Includes setting out of the point and avoiding the existing reinforcement by scanning beforehand, drilling to the diameter and depth specified by the resin manufacturer, cleaning the hole by repeated blowing out and brushing, the operation on which the capacity of the anchor depends entirely and the one most often skipped on site, injecting the resin from the bottom, inserting the bar with a twisting motion and respecting the curing time before loading it. Measured per unit actually constructed.

reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|st.titulo: Strengthening of a slab or beam with a steel section
reinforcements-and-structural-repairs|st.descripcion: Strengthening of a concrete slab or beam with a steel section placed beneath the element, connected with chemical anchors and with a levelling mortar at the interface. It is the quickest solution when the capacity of an existing slab has to be increased without thickening it from above. Includes propping the element to be strengthened beforehand, levelling the soffit, drilling and chemical anchoring, hoisting and offering up the section, filling the interface with non-shrink grout to guarantee the transfer of load, since a section that does not bear does not strengthen, tightening the anchors and anti-corrosion protection. Measured by the length of strengthening actually constructed.

Includes protecting the joinery, the fittings and the footway at the foot of the façade, barring off, washing in panels from the top down, rinsing and collecting the run-off. cleaning-and-facade-treatment|fungicidal.descripcion: Treatment of a façade affected by mould, algae or lichen, by applying a fungicidal and algicidal solution, leaving it to act and rinsing afterwards. Painting over a façade with mould without treating it does not remove it: the fungus stays alive beneath the paint and reappears at the first rainy season, so this treatment is a precondition of any finish. Includes protecting the surroundings and the planting, applying the solution to a dry surface, respecting the contact time indicated, brushing the areas of heaviest growth, rinsing and drying before painting. Measured by the area actually completed.

The choice of product is what decides it: an acid cleaner on marble, polished granite or anodized aluminium causes irreversible damage worse than the original stain, so it is always tried first in a hidden area. Includes identifying the type of stain, the prior trial, protecting the surroundings, application with its contact time, brushing, neutralizing and rinsing thoroughly. cleaning-and-facade-treatment|applicatio.descripcion: Application of a colorless penetrating water repellent to a concrete, facing brick, stone or rendered façade, to reduce the absorption of water without forming a film or altering the appearance. Measured by the area actually constructed.

thermal-and-acoustic-insulation|acoustic.descripcion: Laying mineral wool acoustic insulation in the cavity of plasterboard partitions or suspended ceilings. The insulation absorbs sound energy within the cavity, but its effect is cancelled out if there are rigid bridges or air paths: a back box placed back to back on either side of the partition lets through more noise than the insulation holds back. Includes cutting the boards oversize so that they stay in place by friction without slumping, laying them over the whole cavity leaving no voids and sealing around the service penetrations. thermal-and-acoustic-insulation|reflecti.descripcion: Laying double bubble reflective foil beneath a metal or tiled roof, fixed to the structure with sealed laps. liquid-applied-and-acrylic-waterproofing.titulo: Waterproofing of a buried wall from the inside
liquid-applied-and-acrylic-waterproofing.descripcion: Waterproofing of a buried wall on its internal face with a negative side cementitious mortar, where it is not possible to excavate to treat it from the external face. It works against the pressure of water pushing from outside, a far more demanding situation than conventional waterproofing, so it requires a specific product and a perfectly sound and rough substrate. Includes hacking off the existing rendering back to the substrate, cutting out and opening the pore, plugging active water paths with rapid setting cement, reinforcing the junctions and the coats of negative side mortar. waterproofing-of-wet-areas|waterproofing.titulo: Waterproofing of a bathroom or shower floor beneath the tiling
waterproofing-of-wet-areas|waterproofing.descripcion: Waterproofing of the floor of a bathroom, shower or utility room with a flexible cementitious membrane, with the junctions reinforced and the drain treated, as a base beneath the tiling. It is the layer that holds the water that passes through the ceramic tile and the grout, which are not watertight. The critical point is the junction of the floor with the wall and the collar of the drain: that is where 90 % of the bathrooms that leak to the floor below fail. Includes saturating the substrate, reinforcing every junction with a strip, treating the drain with its collar, the two cross coats and the ponding test before tiling. Measured by the area actually constructed.

waterproofing-of-wet-areas|waterproofing.descripcion: Internal waterproofing of a planter with a flexible cementitious membrane and a drainage layer, including the drain outlet. A planter that is not waterproofed transmits permanent moisture to the adjoining wall and ends up blowing the render and the paint on the opposite face. Includes preparing the inside, reinforcing the junctions and corners, the coats of membrane, treating the drain penetration, laying the geotextile and the gravel drainage layer before the growing medium. waterproofing-of-wet-areas|sealing-of-a-.titulo: Sealing of a pipe penetration in waterproofing
waterproofing-of-wet-areas|sealing-of-a-.descripcion: Sealing of the penetration of a pipe, aerial, support or any element passing through the waterproofing, with a collar, reinforcing strip and elastic mastic. Every penetration is a deliberate hole in the layer that has to be watertight, and dealing with it using a simple bead of silicone is the usual cause of localised leaks. Includes cleaning and preparing around the penetration, fitting the collar or wall sleeve, reinforcing with a strip embedded in the waterproofing, sealing with a compatible elastic mastic and checking. Measured per penetration actually sealed.

waterproofing-of-wet-areas|internal-wate.descripcion: Internal waterproofing of a potable water tank with a cementitious mortar suitable for contact with drinking water, with the junctions reinforced and a watertightness test. The product must be certified for potable water: an ordinary waterproofing compound releases compounds into the water and makes it unfit to drink. Includes emptying and cleaning the tank, cutting out and making good the walls, reinforcing every junction and pipe penetration with a strip, the coats of cementitious mortar, curing, the watertightness test by filling and washing and disinfecting before it is brought into service. Measured by the area actually constructed, deducting voids over 1 m².

bases-sub-bases-and-levelling|preparatio.titulo: Preparation and bonding agent on an existing slab
bases-sub-bases-and-levelling|preparatio.descripcion: Preparation of an existing slab or floor that is to remain as the base, by cleaning, making good and applying a bonding coat, to receive a fill layer or an adhered floor. It is used in refurbishment where the base is not demolished and the new layer has to be guaranteed not to come away. Includes sounding by tapping and making good the hollow areas, degreasing and removing the remains of adhesives or paints, vacuuming up the dust, opening up the pore by rubbing down or light hacking, and applying the bonding coat respecting the open time before receiving the next layer. bases-sub-bases-and-levelling|localised-.titulo: Localised repair and making good of an existing floor
bases-sub-bases-and-levelling|localised-.descripcion: Localised repair of an existing floor by replacing loose, hollow or broken tiles and making good the deteriorated areas, keeping the rest of the floor. This is the intervention that avoids replacing a whole floor over localised damage, and its success depends on having tiles from the same batch or on relocating tiles taken from a hidden area, such as the inside of a wardrobe, because a tile from another batch is obvious from a distance. Includes carefully lifting the affected tiles, cleaning the substrate, replacing them with adhesive, levelling with the adjoining tiles, grouting to match and cleaning. Includes checking the flatness of the substrate beforehand, setting out of the layout, cutting with a water cooled diamond disc cutter, the final cleaning and the removal of debris. The tile is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

ceramic-and-porcelain-tile-floors|cerami.titulo: Ceramic tile flooring in a wet area, laid to fall to the drain
ceramic-and-porcelain-tile-floors|cerami.descripcion: Laying of ceramic or porcelain tiling in a wet area, forming the falls towards the drain and treating the junction with the floor drain. Getting the fall right is what determines whether the water drains away or lies in puddles, a defect that in a shower or a laundry is noticed on the first day of use. Includes setting out of the falls from the edges towards the drain, cutting and fitting the tiles around the drain, back buttering, levelling while keeping the fall, grouting with a mortar suitable for wet areas, and the flexible sealing of the junction with the walls and with the drain. The tile is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

ceramic-and-porcelain-tile-floors|cerami.titulo: Ceramic tile flooring on a terrace or outdoor area
ceramic-and-porcelain-tile-floors|cerami.descripcion: Laying of ceramic or porcelain tiling on a terrace, patio or exterior area, with a high performance cementitious adhesive, a wide joint and movement joints around the perimeter and in the bays. Outdoors the floor suffers thermal movement and moisture beneath the tile, so the wide joint and the movement joints are what prevent tenting and the tiles coming away through the build up of stress. Includes checking the drainage fall of the substrate, setting out, back buttering, forming the movement joints, grouting with an exterior mortar and the perimeter sealing. stone-floors-granite-and-terrazzo|marble.descripcion: Laying of a marble or granite floor in a thin bed with a high performance white cementitious adhesive, with a minimal joint. White adhesive is essential on light marbles because the grey shows through the slab and produces irreversible staining. Includes checking and making the substrate level beforehand, setting out of the layout taking account of the veining and the tone so that the composition runs continuously, back buttering, levelling with wedges, cutting with a water cooled disc, grouting to match and cleaning with non acidic products, since acid attacks marble permanently. The slab is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

stone-floors-granite-and-terrazzo|cast-i.descripcion: Continuous cast in place terrazzo floor, formed by a layer of mortar with marble aggregate, divided into bays by divider strips, with the final grinding and buffing. It is a traditional floor widely used in Venezuela, very durable and with no joints between slabs, and its result depends on the homogeneity of the mix and on how the grinding is carried out. Includes preparing the substrate, setting out and placing the divider strips that absorb the shrinkage and define the bays, pouring and ruling off the aggregate layer, curing, grinding in passes of decreasing grit with water, filling the pores and the final buffing. stone-floors-granite-and-terrazzo|flagst.titulo: Flagstone or irregular natural stone flooring
stone-floors-granite-and-terrazzo|flagst.descripcion: Laying of a flagstone or irregular format natural stone floor, bedded in mortar or a high deformability adhesive depending on the thickness of the piece. As there is no regular layout, the bay is composed piece by piece looking for the fit and the distribution of tones, which noticeably reduces the output. Includes selecting and sorting the material beforehand, setting out of the bay, laying with a controlled irregular joint, grouting, cleaning and applying the water repellent sealer that protects the stone and makes it easier to maintain. stone-floors-granite-and-terrazzo|polish.descripcion: Grinding and buffing of an existing marble, granite or terrazzo floor, to recover the lost shine and to remove surface scratches and stains. It is a very cost effective alternative to replacing the floor, since it restores the original appearance for a fraction of the cost. Includes protecting the surroundings and the skirtings, grinding with successive passes of decreasing grit with water, collecting and removing the slurry generated, filling the pores and small chips, buffing with a crystallizing agent and applying the stain resistant sealer. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

wood-and-laminate-floors|floating-lamina.titulo: Floating laminate flooring with acoustic underlay
wood-and-laminate-floors|floating-lamina.descripcion: Laying of a laminate floating floor on an acoustic underlay, assembled by interlocking without adhesive, with a perimeter expansion gap. The floating system requires the perimeter gap to be left free all round and hidden under the skirting: if the floor is butted tight against the wall, it tents and lifts when it expands. Includes checking the flatness and the moisture of the mortar bed, laying the underlay with sealed laps, setting out of the direction of the boards and the width of the last row, interlocking assembly with perimeter wedges, the adjusting cuts at frames and pipes and removing the wedges. The floor is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

wood-and-laminate-floors|solid-wood-floo.titulo: Solid wood flooring nailed to battens
wood-and-laminate-floors|solid-wood-floo.descripcion: Solid wood board floor nailed to battens fixed to the mortar bed, with a ventilated cavity. It is the traditional solution and the most durable, since solid wood takes several rubbing downs over its life. Includes applying the preservative to the battens and to the underside of the board, setting out and levelling the battens, ventilating the cavity through perimeter grilles, secret nailing the board, the perimeter expansion gap and the trim. The final rubbing down and varnishing are not included and are priced separately. The wood is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

wood-and-laminate-floors|parquet-floorin.titulo: Parquet flooring bonded to the levelling bed
wood-and-laminate-floors|parquet-floorin.descripcion: Laying of parquet glued directly to the mortar bed with a polyurethane adhesive, without battens. It demands a perfectly flat, dry bed with no residual moisture: parquet glued over a damp base tents and comes away beyond remedy, so measuring the moisture of the substrate before laying is not a formality but the condition of the work. Includes checking the flatness and the moisture, priming the substrate if the adhesive requires it, setting out of the layout, gluing and laying under pressure, the perimeter gap and the removal of adhesive residue. Rubbing down and varnishing are not included. The parquet is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

wood-and-laminate-floors|rubbing-down-an.titulo: Rubbing down and varnishing of a wood floor
wood-and-laminate-floors|rubbing-down-an.descripcion: Rubbing down and finishing of a new or existing wood floor with polyurethane varnish, in three coats with rubbing down between coats. On existing floors this operation fully restores the appearance of the wood and avoids replacing it. Includes punching down any nails that stand proud and filling the joints and cracks with filler to match, rubbing down in passes of decreasing grit with a belt sander and an edger at the perimeters and in the corners, thorough vacuuming between passes because any particle ends up trapped under the varnish, applying the coats of varnish with a light rubbing down between them, and respecting the drying times before walking on it. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

wood-and-laminate-floors|timber-or-compo.descripcion: Exterior deck floor with treated or engineered wood boards, mounted on battens with a gap between boards for drainage and ventilation. The gap between boards and the ventilation underneath are not aesthetic: they are what allows the water to drain away and the wood to dry out, preventing rot. Includes setting out and levelling the battens with a drainage fall, applying the preservative to the cuts and to the end grain, fixing the boards with a hidden clip or stainless steel screws, keeping a constant gap with a spacer and the perimeter trim. vinyl-and-resilient-floors|sheet-vinyl-f.descripcion: Laying of a continuous sheet vinyl floor, glued to the mortar bed, with the joints between sheets welded or sealed. Its advantage over tile is the almost total absence of joints, which makes it ideal in areas with demanding hygiene requirements. It needs a perfectly smooth substrate, since vinyl is a thin material that copies and makes visible any grain or irregularity in the bed. Includes the fine levelling beforehand if the substrate needs it, cutting and laying out the sheets and leaving them to relax, gluing, rolling to remove the air, welding or sealing the joints and the perimeter trim. The material is selected by the client and priced separately. Measured by the area actually completed, deducting openings over 1 m².

vinyl-and-resilient-floors|vinyl-tile-or.descripcion: Laying of a vinyl floor in tile or plank form, LVT type, self adhesive, glued or interlocking depending on the system. It combines the ease of replacing piece by piece with an appearance very close to that of wood or stone. Includes checking the flatness, cleanliness and moisture of the substrate, setting out of the layout to centre the bay and avoid narrow pieces at the edges, laying with a butt joint, rolling on the glued systems, the adjusting cuts at frames and pipes, and the perimeter trim. Includes preparing and levelling the substrate, cutting and laying out the material and leaving it to relax so that it recovers its dimension before fixing, gluing, rolling, adjusting and sealing the joints, and the perimeter trim with a cove or a profile. Includes checking that the substrate is clean and dry, laying the underlay where the system requires it, cutting and laying out the lengths respecting the direction of the pile, which must be the same throughout the room because otherwise the lengths read as different tones, gluing or stretching, sealing the seams and the trim at thresholds and around the perimeter. continuous-concrete-and-microcement-floo.descripcion: Continuous concrete floor with a mechanically power troweled finish, with sawn control joints and curing. Includes pouring and ruling off the concrete, the initial floating, the power trowelling in as many passes as needed to obtain the texture and the closing of the pore required, sawing the control joints at the moment when the concrete will take it without spalling or cracking, and curing, which on a power troweled floor is decisive because all the surface quality is lost if the mix water evaporates too quickly. continuous-concrete-and-microcement-floo.descripcion: Concrete floor with a stamped finish by means of textured mats and a pigmented release agent, with a final sealing. Includes pouring and ruling off, applying the powdered colour hardener, dusting on the pigmented release agent, stamping with the mats at the exact point of set, a narrow window of time on which the whole result depends, sawing the joints, washing off the excess release agent and applying the coats of sealer. continuous-concrete-and-microcement-floo.descripcion: Continuous microcement covering over an existing floor or mortar bed, applied in coats with reinforcing mesh and sealed with several coats of protective varnish. It allows a floor to be renewed without demolishing it and with hardly any gain in level, which in refurbishment resolves the problem of thresholds and doors. It is very sensitive to the substrate: any crack or movement shows through in the finish.
